title: A section of an invertible sheaf avoids any finite set on an affine scheme
statement: Let $X$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and let $E\subseteq |X|$ be a finite set of points, not necessarily closed. There exists $s\in\Gamma(X,L)$ such that, for every $x\in E$, the image of its germ $s_x$ in $L_x/\mathfrak m_xL_x$ is nonzero. Here $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is the local ring, $\mathfrak m_x$ its maximal ideal, and $\kappa(x)=\mathcal O_{X,x}/\mathfrak m_x$ is the residue field [def-weil-residue-field].

proof.text:
Put $A=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and identify the affine scheme $X$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Write $\mathfrak p_x$ for the prime corresponding to $x$. The affine stalk-localization statement [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], applied with $U=X$, identifies the germ map with $A	o A_{\mathfrak p_x}$. Thus for $a\in A$ its residue $a(x)$ is nonzero exactly when $a
otin\mathfrak p_x$. Explicitly, $a
otin\mathfrak p_x$ gives a unit germ. Conversely, if $a\in\mathfrak p_x$ and its germ were a unit, represent an inverse as $b/c$ with $c
otin\mathfrak p_x$. Equality $ab/c=1$ gives $u(ab-c)=0$ for some $u
otin\mathfrak p_x$, forcing $uc=uab\in\mathfrak p_x$, a contradiction. In a local ring, zero residue is exactly membership in its maximal ideal, equivalently failure to be a unit.

source.place: Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves (1),(6); affine coordinate preparation for Properties 0F20

proof.text: The sheaf $L$ is quasi-coherent by [def-sc-invertible-module]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-algebra-module-generators] with $S=X$, the algebra sheaf $\mathcal A=\mathcal O_X$ with its identity structure map, the affine open $U=X$, and $M=L$. Restriction of scalars is the identity, so its quasi-coherence hypothesis holds, and $L$ is generated by global sections. Now [lem-sc-global-generation-nonvanishing-cover] gives $X=\bigcup_t X_t$, where $X_t=\{x:t(x)\ne0\}$. Consequently for every point $x$ there is a global section $t$ with $t(x)\ne0$. Here $t(x)$ denotes the class of $t_x$ in $L_x/\mathfrak m_xL_x$.

source.place: Tag 0F20, lemma-quasi-affine-invertible-nonvanishing-section, base case: global generation; in the affine case use Schemes 01IB, lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent

proof.text: Prove the assertion for every finite subset $E$ by strong induction on $|E|$. For $E=\varnothing$ take $s=0$. Each nonvanishing locus $X_s$ is open by [lem-weil-pbc-nonvanishing-section-trivializes]. If distinct $x,y\in E$ satisfy $x\leadsto y$, apply the induction hypothesis to $E\setminus\{x\}$. Its section is nonzero at $y$; every open containing $y$ contains its generalization $x$, by the definition of specialization, so the section is also nonzero at $x$. This handles any pair of comparable points. It remains to handle a nonempty $E$ with no specializations between distinct points.

source.place: Tag 0F20, lemma-quasi-affine-invertible-nonvanishing-section, empty case and induction step removing a generalization; Modules 01CY supplies openness

proof.text: Choose $z\in E$ and put $F=E\setminus\{z\}$. By induction there is $s\in\Gamma(X,L)$ nonzero at all points of $F$. If $s(z)\ne0$ we are done. Otherwise $s(z)=0$. By step 2 choose $t\in\Gamma(X,L)$ with $t(z)\ne0$. In the case $F=\varnothing$, this already proves the assertion; the same construction below also works with its empty product equal to $1$.

source.place: Tag 0F20, lemma-quasi-affine-invertible-nonvanishing-section, induction step: the old section and a section nonvanishing at the new point

proof.text:
For each $x\in F$ we have $\mathfrak p_x
ot\subseteq\mathfrak p_z$: inclusion would imply $x\leadsto z$. Indeed the Zariski closed sets are $V(I)=\{\mathfrak q:I\subseteq\mathfrak q\}$, so any closed set containing $\mathfrak p_x$ also contains every prime above it. Choose $a_x\in\mathfrak p_x\setminus\mathfrak p_z$ and let $f=\prod_{x\in F}a_x\in A$. For each $x\in F$, one factor lies in $\mathfrak p_x$, hence $f\in\mathfrak p_x$. Every factor is outside the prime $\mathfrak p_z$, hence $f
otin\mathfrak p_z$. The scalar-residue criterion in step 1 therefore gives $f(x)=0$ for $x\in F$ and $f(z)
e0$. This is the affine separating-function construction in the induction of the source, written directly using prime ideals.

source.place: Tag 0F20, lemma-quasi-affine-invertible-nonvanishing-section, induction step: choose a section supported away from the closures of the earlier points; the affine separating scalar is the explicit product above

proof.text: Set $v=s+ft\in\Gamma(X,L)$. Taking germs and then quotienting by the maximal ideal commutes with addition and scalar multiplication, so $v(x)=s(x)+f(x)t(x)$. For $x\in F$ this is $s(x)\ne0$. At $z$ it is $f(z)t(z)\ne0$: multiplication by a nonzero element of the field $\kappa(z)$ is invertible on the vector space $L_z/\mathfrak m_zL_z$. Thus $v$ is nonzero at every point of $E$. This completes the induction, including arbitrary nonclosed points, and proves precisely the asserted residue-fibre nonvanishing.
